discoveries.headline: Before you buy crypto, read this
discoveries.why: Moneysmart, the government's free money guide, sets out the basics plainly: crypto is very volatile, it isn't legal tender in Australia, and many platforms aren't licensed, so you may not be protected if one fails or is hacked. The real story of Rhett, who lost $97,000 to a fake endorsement, shows how scams work. Education, not advice.

discoveries.headline: If Not Now: an anthem for a reef
discoveries.why: More than 20 Australian artists, with Jimmy Barnes and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard out front and John Butler, Montaigne, Alex Lahey, Urthboy, DOBBY and Fred Leone among them, have reimagined King Gizzard's Environmental Music Prize-winning song for the Save Scott Reef campaign. The campaign, from Greenpeace Australia Pacific, Green Music Australia and p(doom) Records, says Woodside plans up to 57 wells under and around the reef off Western Australia, and half a million Australians have asked the government to stop it. It's out now on all the usual music apps; the story is here.
discoveries.meta_credit: Greenpeace Australia Pacific · Green Music Australia · p(doom) Records · art by Jonathan Zawada

discoveries.headline: Landscapes with nothing faked
discoveries.why: The Natural Landscape Photography Awards check every finalist's RAW file, so what you see is what was really there. Lukas Furlan was named Photographer of the Year for a set that moves from tiny ice details to mountain vistas, and Abraham Saikley took Photograph of the Year for a jagged mountain range. Nearly 12,000 entries from 52 countries; a slow scroll is a good start to a Monday.
discoveries.credit: © Lukas Furlan (Photographer of the Year) and Abraham Saikley (Photograph of the Year), Natural Landscape Photography Awards; each photographer credited in the captions

discoveries.headline: The Compassionate Mind, in 90 seconds
discoveries.why: This week's quote comes from the Dalai Lama's message on compassion. In this short clip, recorded in New Delhi in 2010, he explains why a compassionate mind is the root of inner peace, and how fear, anger and distrust grow when we only think of ourselves. Watch it, then carry one kind act into your week.
discoveries.source: The Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama
discoveries.meta_credit: dalailama.com · His Holiness the Dalai Lama

quote.text: The more we care for the happiness of others, the greater our own sense of well-being becomes.

discoveries.headline: Jay Shetty: stop waiting to figure it out
discoveries.why: Jay Shetty's live show played Sydney on Saturday and reaches Brisbane tonight, built around four decisions: how you see yourself, how you make money, who you love and how you serve. This episode of On Purpose is a good way in: purpose isn't found in one flash, it's built through curiosity and small steps, and he gives you something to try in the next 48 hours. Perfect for the commute.
discoveries.meta_credit: On Purpose with Jay Shetty · Rolling Stone Australia (tour dates)

discoveries.headline: The Bangalow Show turns 125
discoveries.why: The first show was held in March 1897 on Robert Campbell's land, with about 300 people on day one and 800 on day two. It was cancelled in 1917 and 1947 and twice for COVID, and it still runs on about 25 committee members and more than 100 volunteers, with the Written Word and Art sections the pavilion's favourites. Congratulations to Dave Copeland, winner of this year's Bush Poet competition, and to runner-up Lisa Wade, UBUNBOUND's founder, whose playful poem is built on the letters of phone keys 1, 2 and 5, plus 'bush'. Read the full poem on the reader site.
discoveries.meta_credit: North Coast Times · Penelope Shaw · Bangalow Show Society

quote.text: Still, sweet / Home / Yes everlasting, / Years - Happy, home - US
quote.by: Lisa Wade, runner-up, Bush Poet competition

discoveries.headline: Ayurveda's guide to every season
discoveries.why: Ayurvedic practitioner Kathryn Templeton explains how the three doshas map onto the year: vata from late autumn into early winter, kapha from deep winter into spring, pitta from late spring into early autumn. In Sydney we're heading into pitta season, so look for her cooling rituals, like sheetali breathing. General information, not medical advice.

discoveries.headline: A gentle morning practice, bed or mat
discoveries.why: Trauma-informed teacher Kassandra Mollé talks you through 17 minutes of cyclic sighing, cat-cow, sphinx, half frog and soft spinal twists, ending in rest. It's audio only, so close your eyes and follow her voice. A kind way to begin the week.
discoveries.meta_credit: The Calm Lab Podcast · Kassandra Mollé

discoveries.headline: How little strength training is enough?
discoveries.why: McMaster kinesiology researchers explain that one weekly session with lighter weights, taken to fatigue at around 20 to 25 reps, builds both muscle and strength. Their best line: the threshold that matters most isn't between good and excellent, it's between zero and one. Start this week.
discoveries.meta_credit: McMaster University · Tom Janssen & Matthew Lees (via The Conversation)
